text: 75 Guidance for national tuberculosis programmes on the management of tuberculosis in children 8. Implementation and management by NTP; integrated care 8.1 Chapter objectives Chapter 8 outlines the responsibilities of the NTP for implementing childhood TB activities according to national guidelines and in line with this second edition of Guidance for national tuberculosis programmes on the management of tuberculosis in children. It outlines actions needed at global and national levels and discusses the importance of an integrated, family-oriented approach to TB in children. 8.2 Action at the global level At the global level, implementation and evaluation of this updated guidance may include the following: l WHO and partners providing training and monitoring tools for child TB and child contact management, and fostering their uptake and use. l WHO adjusting indicators to capture the data needed to evaluate child TB activities, including contact investigation and outcomes. l WHO and partners facilitating access to diagnostic tools for children, and fostering their uptake and use. l WHO and partners assisting countries to establish drug resistance surveys of new patients, including all children of all ages and adolescents. l The Global Drug Facility (GDF) responding to the need for anti-TB drugs and preventive therapy for children, providing guidance to countries on the transition from old to new dosages and regimens. l WHO and partners assisting countries in securing funding for, planning, implementing and evaluating these activities. 8.3 Next steps at national level NTP actions at the national level l Development of national child TB guidelines, either as one section of the NTP guidelines or as separate guidelines, linking them with Integrated Management of Childhood Illness and translating them into appropriate languages as needed. l Formation of a child TB working group within the NTP, with representation from community and national child TB experts as well as from the NTP. l Evaluation of surveillance data to target particular settings for implementation and assessment of specific activities.
